conclusion: Adding H&E pathology images to the available clinical variables (including hormone and growth-factor receptor statuses) improves four-class PAM50 prediction in this labelled TCGA-BRCA cohort of {{n_patients}} patients. Under the evaluator's unified patient-level protocol, the selected model, {{selected_plan}} ({{selected_name}}), increased out-of-fold macro-averaged F-score from {{clinical_f1}} for the tuned clinical-only baseline to {{selected_f1}}, a paired gain of {{true_gain}}. This improvement is supported with high statistical certainty within the cohort: the patient-level paired bootstrap confidence interval extends from {{true_ci_low}} to {{true_ci_high}}, lying strictly above zero, and agrees with the internal nested cross-validation estimate of {{selected_plan}} ({{self_gain}}, confidence interval {{self_ci_low}} to {{self_ci_high}}) as well as positive confidence intervals in {{n_ci_above_zero}} of the {{n_candidates}} evaluated plans.

At the same time, unified benchmarking highlights clear limits to tournament selection and architectural complexity. Although {{selected_plan}} won the pairwise tournament, it ranked at position {{selected_true_rank}} out of {{n_candidates}} under the unified evaluator, trailing the top-scoring candidate {{best_true_plan}} by {{selection_gap}}. Moreover, {{selected_plan}} is a simple PCA-reduced patient-mean logistic fusion model that does not outperform an unreduced simple mean-pooled logistic reference ({{reference_gain}}), and only {{n_beating_reference}} of the {{n_candidates}} candidates—despite {{n_ambitious}} ambitious deep and ensemble designs—achieved a larger unified gain than {{reference_gain}}.

The paired gain persisted at {{site_gain}} when entire collection sites were held out during validation, although residual technical site confounding cannot be fully excluded. These findings establish incremental patient-level PAM50 predictive value from H&E slides alongside routine clinical covariates in this TCGA-BRCA cohort only; they do not establish standalone H&E predictive utility, biological mechanisms linking tissue morphology to transcriptomic subtypes, statistically proven per-class gains, or generalisability to external clinical populations.
evidence: Across {{n_patients}} labelled TCGA-BRCA patients, {{selected_plan}} ({{selected_name}}) tested incremental multimodal fusion within repeated patient-level nested cross-validation without using RNA-derived variables, collection-site predictors, external annotations, or evaluation-fold leakage. Within each training fold, identical missing-indicator clinical encodings were paired with PCA-reduced slide-mean H&E features from an inner-selected pathology foundation encoder and fit with class-balanced logistic regression alongside a tuned clinical-only counterpart. Under the unified evaluation protocol, adding H&E features raised macro-averaged F-score from {{clinical_f1}} to {{selected_f1}}, giving a paired gain of {{true_gain}} (patient-level bootstrap confidence interval {{true_ci_low}} to {{true_ci_high}}). In its own validation, {{selected_plan}} reported a gain of {{self_gain}} (confidence interval {{self_ci_low}} to {{self_ci_high}}), a self-minus-unified difference of {{selected_inflation}} that yielded the same qualitative conclusion.

The frozen pool contained {{n_candidates}} candidate plans: the simple reference fusion plan {{selected_plan}} and {{n_ambitious}} ambitious architectures spanning residual tile-attention multiple-instance learning (P2), unlabelled-PCA multi-encoder gated hierarchical fusion (P3), morphological-prototype boosted-tree stacking (P4), clinical-query cross-attention transformers (P5), and semi-supervised pre-adapted tile aggregation (P6). Across {{n_matches}} judged tournament matches with {{order_consistency}} order consistency, {{tournament_champion}} ranked at the top and passed audit without blocking defects. Under the unified evaluator, however, {{selected_plan}} ranked at position {{selected_true_rank}} rather than at the top, falling short of {{best_true_plan}} by {{selection_gap}}, while candidate self-reports across the pool exceeded unified gains by an average of {{mean_inflation}}.

Results across all {{n_candidates}} candidates confirm a consistent multimodal signal while showing that complex tile-level modelling added negligible value over global feature averaging. Specifically, {{n_positive}} of the {{n_candidates}} plans achieved positive unified gains over the clinical-only baseline and {{n_ci_above_zero}} produced unified bootstrap confidence intervals strictly above zero. Yet the evaluator's unreduced simple mean-pooled logistic reference already achieved a unified gain of {{reference_gain}}; {{selected_plan}} ({{true_gain}}) did not establish an advantage over this simple baseline, and only {{n_beating_reference}} candidates in the pool beat {{reference_gain}}.

Unified class-level recall changes with H&E fusion were positive in point estimate for every subtype—{{recall_change_LumB}} for LumB, {{recall_change_Her2}} for the growth-factor-receptor-enriched subtype, {{recall_change_LumA}} for LumA, and {{recall_change_Basal}} for Basal—but these subgroup differences lack multiplicity-adjusted uncertainty intervals and are not statistically established. Because pretrained pathology features strongly reflect contributing institutions whose subtype mix is uneven, {{selected_plan}} was further evaluated by holding out entire collection sites from training folds. The paired macro F-score gain remained {{site_gain}} under site-held-out validation, showing that the improvement persisted across unseen collection sites even though site confounding cannot be fully excluded.
limits: This analysis is confined to incremental multimodal PAM50 prediction across {{n_patients}} labelled patients in TCGA-BRCA and does not establish standalone H&E predictive utility, biological mechanisms, or generalisability to external clinical cohorts.

Although the multimodal gain persisted at {{site_gain}} when whole collection sites were held out, foundation-model image features strongly encode institution-specific technical variation associated with subtype prevalence, so site confounding is not fully excluded.

Substantial missing and equivocal clinical receptor entries—particularly for growth-factor receptor status—may exaggerate the incremental benefit of H&E morphology compared with clinical workflows that have complete, standardised immunohistochemistry panels.

Cohort class imbalance leaves the smallest PAM50 subtypes sparse, and the observed per-class recall shifts ({{recall_change_LumB}} for LumB, {{recall_change_Her2}} for the growth-factor-receptor-enriched class, {{recall_change_LumA}} for LumA, and {{recall_change_Basal}} for Basal) are descriptive point estimates rather than statistically established effects.

The selected plan ({{selected_plan}}) ranked at position {{selected_true_rank}} behind {{best_true_plan}} by {{selection_gap}} under the unified evaluator and failed to outperform the unreduced simple mean-pooled logistic reference ({{reference_gain}}), while slide-mean pooling ignores spatial heterogeneity across varying tile counts and multiple slides per patient.

Screening {{n_candidates}} candidate pipelines across multiple high-dimensional image encoders introduced model-selection multiplicity and slight average self-reported score inflation ({{mean_inflation}}) relative to the unified benchmark.
recommendations: Evaluate the {{selected_plan}} clinical-plus-H&E logistic fusion model in external, multi-institutional breast cancer cohorts with complete, centrally standardised receptor measurements to test whether the {{true_gain}} incremental gain generalises outside TCGA-BRCA.

Adopt regularised patient-mean feature fusion as the standard multimodal baseline before deploying complex tile-level networks, given that only {{n_beating_reference}} of {{n_candidates}} candidates exceeded the {{reference_gain}} simple reference gain and {{best_true_plan}} improved over {{selected_plan}} by only {{selection_gap}}.

Pair routine site-held-out validation with stain normalisation or site-invariant representation alignment to reduce institutional batch signals beyond the current {{site_gain}} site-held-out sensitivity check.

Perform adequately powered, multiplicity-controlled subgroup and complete-case receptor analyses in larger cohorts to test whether descriptive recall increases such as {{recall_change_LumB}} in LumB represent reproducible class-specific gains.
